title: Buy the next drink
invitation: Pay for whoever is behind you in line. Leave before they notice.

title: Tip more than you meant to
invitation: Round up. Then round up again. Someone's day changes and you'll never know it.

title: Give something away
invitation: A book, a tool, a plant — something you own that someone else would actually use. Today.

title: Cover something small
invitation: Pick up a coffee, a parking fee, a lunch for someone. Don't mention it afterwards.

title: Donate a lunch
invitation: Give away what you'd have spent on lunch. Eat something simple instead.

title: Send one message
invitation: Someone you haven't spoken to in months. No agenda, no ask. Just that you thought of them.

title: Call, don't text
invitation: One person, five minutes, your actual voice.

title: Name the thing
invitation: Tell someone what you appreciate about them — the specific thing, not the general feeling.

title: Wait for the second answer
invitation: Ask someone how they are. When they say fine, stay quiet long enough for the real answer.

title: Thank someone late
invitation: A teacher, a former boss, someone who helped years ago. Tell them it mattered.

title: Introduce two people
invitation: You know two people who should know each other. Make the introduction today.

title: Check on the quiet one
invitation: Someone has gone quiet lately. Ask after them, without making it a thing.

title: Let someone ahead
invitation: In line, in traffic, in conversation. Give up the space you were entitled to.

title: Leave one argument unwon
invitation: You could be right today. Choose not to need it.

title: Give the benefit of the doubt
invitation: Someone will annoy you today. Assume the version of the story where they're doing their best.

title: Phone down, all the way down
invitation: Every conversation today, the phone stays out of your hand. Not face-down on the table. Away.

title: Forgive one small thing
invitation: Something you've been carrying that isn't worth its weight. Put it down quietly. No one needs to be told.

title: One meal, no screen
invitation: Just the food, and whoever is with you. Notice how long it takes to stop reaching.

title: Take the long way
invitation: A different route home. Find five things you've never noticed on the usual one.

title: Three minutes before
invitation: Sit for three minutes before your first meeting. No screen, no notes, no input.

title: Sixty seconds of sky
invitation: Step outside. Look up. Stay there a full minute — it's longer than you think.

title: Do one thing at half speed
invitation: Pick a task you usually rush. Take twice as long on purpose.

title: The first hour
invitation: No screen for the first hour you're awake. Let the day start on your terms.

title: Thank someone invisible
invitation: The cleaner, the driver, the person at the counter. Use their name if you can find it.

title: Compliment a stranger
invitation: One sincere thing, said out loud, expecting nothing back.

title: Praise in public
invitation: Credit someone's work today where other people can hear it.

title: Say the hard thing kindly
invitation: There's something true you've been avoiding saying. Say it gently, or let it go entirely — but stop carrying it.

title: Ask the question
invitation: The one you've been talking yourself out of. Ask it today.

title: Write it, don't say it
invitation: Put the appreciation in writing. People keep what they can re-read.

title: Do it before you're asked
invitation: The chore no one wants. Handle it before anyone brings it up.

title: Hold the door
invitation: For the person whose hands are full. Then wait for the next one too.

title: Carry something
invitation: Someone today is holding more than they can manage. Take one thing from them.

title: Pick up one piece
invitation: One piece of litter that isn't yours. Leave the place slightly better than you found it.

title: Take something off their plate
invitation: Quietly absorb one task from someone who's underwater. Don't announce it.

title: Offer the seat
invitation: Before you're asked, before it's obvious. Stand up.

title: Three things
invitation: Before you sleep, name three things today gave you. Small ones count most.

title: Thank your body
invitation: One thing it did for you today without being asked. Acknowledge it.

title: Who made today easier
invitation: Someone did. Work out who, then tell them.

title: The best part of your day
invitation: Ask your child what theirs was. Then answer the same question honestly yourself.

title: Let them choose
invitation: Dinner, the music, the route. Hand over one decision today and mean it.

title: One kind thing, together
invitation: Do something small for a neighbour with your child. Let them see the whole thing.

title: Leave a note
invitation: Write or draw something and hide it where someone will find it later.

title: One thing you noticed
invitation: At bedtime, tell them one specific thing they did well today. Specific matters more than big.
